story_text.value:
Crack Attack! is a classic open source puzzle game that's included in many Linux distro repositories. I first played it around 20 years ago, and I've been hooked since.

I wanted to see if an LLM could port it to run in the browser. I suggested recompiling it with Emscripten, but the LLM decided to rewrite it in TypeScript instead, using the original code as a reference. I had to prompt it a bunch to fix some gameplay and rendering differences, but I think the current version is very close to the original.

Anyway, maybe some of you remember this game and will want to try this version.

Play the game: https://leifkb.github.io/crack-attack-browser/ Look at the code: https://github.com/leifkb/crack-attack-browser/

title.value: Show HN: Crack Attack game vibe-ported to run in browser

story_text.value:
Hi HN, I’ve made a Mac launcher that runs JS scripts. There are the usual scripts for opening applications and finding emojis, but you can also `cd` around and run scripts in the working folder (there are built-in scripts for copying, moving and deleting, and I’ve made my own custom scripts to e.g. clear out build artifacts). It’s kind of half launcher/half command line.

- 100% Mac native

- Your scripts live in ~/Launch (or another folder if you prefer)

- You can connect to a Git backend (my script files are connected to a private GitHub repo)

- You can write your own scripts to do anything that JavaScript can do (with some node polyfills for fs and fetch)

- Autocomplete and help text for scripts and script arguments

There's a 7 day trial download or a $12 once off purchase.

I hope you like it!

story_text.value:
I frequently write my documents in LaTeX. A long time ago I moved all my documents from Overleaf to offline due to the compile limit. However, I miss the visual editor and real-time collaboration. I tried Live Share before but it is super buggy. So this is the original reason Texpile was made.

Besides the features in your standard LaTeX editor such as Overleaf / LaTeX Workshop / TeXstudio, you also get these:

- Real-time LaTeX preview (like Typst's instant preview)

- Visual editor

- End-to-end encrypted real-time collaboration.

- You can directly paste images into the file explorer

And a few other features that most LaTeX editors have: SyncTeX, git diff view, spell checker, formatter, etc.

title.value: Show HN: Texpile, an open-source desktop LaTeX editor with a visual mode

story_text.value:
Hi HN!

Not every internet radio station is listed in a directory like Radio Browser. For a lot of them, the only way to actually listen is to dig the stream URL (.mp3/.aac/.m3u8) out of the station's website by hand — and that's before you even find a player that isn't full of ads or locked to its own catalog.

Freqcast lets you paste the station's website instead of the stream URL directly. It first checks the Radio Browser catalog, then scans the website itself, discovers a playable stream, verifies that it works, and adds it to your library. In many cases, you never have to hunt for the URL yourself.

No ads, no tracking, no account — everything lives locally in the app. Your station list can be exported as JSON, and imported from JSON, OPML, M3U, or PLS.

No Play Store listing — grab the APK from Releases. F-Droid submission is in progress.

Would genuinely love feedback!

title.value: Show HN: Freqcast, an Android radio player that finds streams from a website URL

story_text.value:
I remember being able to play poker and trivia with random strangers on cross country flights on the IFE screens. For some reason, they took that away, so I decided to make some myself.

The first two games are here: Poker - https://apps.apple.com/us/app/airplane-mode-poker/id67912479... https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=de.testco.airp... Liar's Dice https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=de.testco.airp... [iOS still in review]

BLE was the choice to have it work cross-platform and support multiple players. There is no Internet access and there is no analytics or app tracking.

It costs $2.99 as a one time unlock to host and $0 to join a game.

Thoughts on other games?

title.value: Show HN: Poker and Liar's Dice over Bluetooth Low Energy

story_text.value:
For whatever reason it has become really hard to transfer very large files with the modern Internet. Usually you end up with paying some cloud provider to store the files so that somebody else can download them. But this is not how it has to be. I've been building Mirall to actually that problem. Mirall is a peer-to-peer application that enables the secure transfer of very large files, hundreds of gigabytes or even terabytes between two computers without any third-party servers or middlemen.

The idea to build Mirall was born at the Mallorca Film Festival. Companies and individuals in the movie industry often have the challenge to transfer large data files during the post production phase of a movie while large production studios often offer their own file transfer solutions. Smaller companies or individuals are often relying on consumer grade third party services, usually this is not allowed because of the potential of data leaks. Somehow it has become a complex problem to transfer large files over the internet. I overheard conversations where this was discussed and thought to myself that I might be able to solve that problem. Having used the Keet app and with some basic understanding of what the Pear framework is able to offer from a capability perspective, I thought I might give it a try.

Over the past four months I've been busy building this app with a high focus on ease of use and security. Now it is out there. The app is open source and free to download and use. I hope it solves a problem for many of you out there. Please give it a try and let me know if it works for you or where to improve.

Oliver

title.value: Show HN: Mirall – Secure large (terabyte) file transfer. No cloud. No middleman
